title: Client Integration Tactical Handoff — Q4 Sprint
content:
Meeting objective: Rapid tactical handoff for Veridian integration (customer stage: pilot -> limited prod). Align SRE, SE, and ProServices on roll/rollback plan, outstanding technical blockers, and short-term support coverage (24x7 on first 72h of canary).

Attendees: Aisha (lead SE), Marco (ProServices), Claire (SRE), Devon (Platform eng), Samir (customer success), Priya (security).

Quick status summary (as of 2026-12-09):
- Pilot environment: green for basic inference flows; load test at 80% of target QPS shows steady latency at p50=120ms, p95=310ms.
- Private deployment (customer VPC): VPC peering established but intermittent route propagation observed.
- KMS integration: customer KMS policy blocks decrypt on second tier; workaround implemented using temporary service account key (temporary, must be replaced).
- Model variant: using alpaca-13b-quant-v2 for cost predictability; accuracy regression vs. baseline within acceptable thresholds for 9/10 prompts in eval suite.

Key decisions made in meeting:
1) Proceed with staged canary rollout on 2026-12-12 08:00 PST (canary window 24h, then 72h expanded coverage if stable).
2) Use soft-fail fallback to hosted smaller variant (7B) if KV cache errors exceed threshold (see INT-912).
3) Temporary KMS service-account key approved for canary only; rotate to customer-managed KMS workflow before full prod (deadline below).

Action items (owner / due / notes):
- Claire H.: Work with cloud networking (ticket NET-2203) to add explicit static routes and run propagation tests; due 2026-12-10. Notes: try manual route refresh after peering acceptance window.
- Marco R.: Create PS runbook excerpt for on-call rotation and escalation matrix for first 72h canary; due 2026-12-11. Include Slack playbook messages and PagerDuty escalation steps.
- Devon O.: Patch runtime to add defensive abort for corrupted KV cache entries and ship hotfix (runtime v0.9.4-hotfix1); due 2026-12-11 EOD. Must include unit test reproducer based on failing trace in SE-4582.
- Priya D.: Finalize KMS policy changes with customer security and audit the temporary service-account key; confirm rotation schedule; due 2026-12-14.
- Aisha P.: Run targeted evaluation subset (50 prompts) comparing outputs from 13B-quant-v2 vs. 7B-fallback and produce delta report for product team; due 2026-12-11 morning.
- Samir K.: Confirm customer-run E2E smoke tests and list of golden prompts; due 2026-12-10.

Open blockers / risks (severity and mitigation):
- VPC route flaps (severity: high) -> mitigation: manual route pinning + SRE watch, postpone full prod until 72h stable.
- KMS decrypt failure under high concurrency (severity: high) -> mitigation: use temporary key + rate-limit KMS calls in SDK and add exponential backoff.
- Quantization mismatch causes occasional hallucination (severity: medium) -> mitigation: whitelist critical prompt families to run on full-precision hosted variant during canary.
- Observability gaps: missing token-level breakdown for one route in console (severity: medium) -> mitigation: Devon to add trace hook and Claire to add dashboard tile (tracked INT-912).

Canary rollout plan (tactical):
- 2026-12-12 08:00 PST: start canary at 2% traffic -> monitor latency, error-rate, quality regressions.
- 2026-12-12 12:00 PST: if stable, move to 10% traffic and enable SLO alerts.
- 2026-12-12 20:00 PST: expand to 30% only if no degradation.
- 2026-12-13 08:00 PST: 72h observation window begins. Any P1 -> immediate rollback to prior routing (automated via rollback playbook).

Rollback playbook (short form):
- Trigger: p95 latency > 500ms for 15m OR error-rate > 2% for 10m OR quality alerts (human flag)
- Steps: 1) Trigger rollback flag in console (DevOps runbook) -> route all traffic to 7B-fallback variant. 2) Notify customer success + account owner (Samir). 3) Open hotfix ticket and attach traces. 4) Start incident bridge (owner: Claire).

Monitoring & observability checklist:
- Token-level and model-level cost tag: present for canary routes (Devon).
- Evals running every 2h comparing golden prompts (Aisha).
- Alert rules: p95 latency, error-rate, QoQ quality regression on golden prompts (Claire).
- Trace retention for 7 days for canary traces (SRE to confirm).

Meeting notes / ad-hoc items (informal):
- "Notes to self": ask product to lock critical prompt set; otherwise we get noisy false positives in quality alerts.
- Marco: remind the field team to prepare customer-facing comms templates for 2-hour incident and 24-hour RCA.
- Quick wins: enable KV prefix caching on test cluster; small change, big improvement for tail latency.
- Outstanding: customer is requesting FIPS-enabled TLS for KMS channel (Priya to validate feasibility).

Links referenced during the meeting: JIRA SE-4582 (KV cache corruption traces), INT-912 (observability gaps), GitHub PR 87 (config for veridian). Slack thread: #se-proservices-veridian-thread (pinned messages have runbook excerpts).

Next sync: 2026-12-11 09:00 PST (pre-canary checkpoint) — agenda: final readiness, network test results, canary observability smoke test.

Appendix — quick command snippets (developer scratchpad):
- Route refresh: `gcloud compute routes import --source=...` (note: customer uses Azure; reworded steps in runbook)
- KMS test: small script to run parallel decrypts (used to reproduce race in SE-4582).

Action owner check (for the scribbler):
- Confirmed with Claire offline that SRE will cover first 48h nights (Claire to escalate to on-call rota).
- Marco will supply the PS on-call list and slack escalation stickers by 2026-12-11 noon.

Unresolved questions (to carry into pre-canary checkpoint):
- Can we remove temporary service-account key earlier if customer upgrades KMS policy? (Priya to confirm)
- Are there any latency-sensitive customers behind the same shared routing? (Devon to validate isolation guarantees)

-- end of notes --

(rough/draft doc — intended as tactical working copy for SE/ProServices handoff; please add inline comments and update action items directly in this doc)
